Afrique du Sud.name: South Africa
hello: “hi, how’s it going?”, the South African beach greeting
food: Braai
The South African barbecue, with boerewors and grilled snoek.
Afrique du Sud.respect: Find out about shark activity and follow the Shark Spotters’ flags. Leave nothing visible in your car.

sea.title: The Sardine Run
sea.text: From May to July, sardine shoals travel up the KwaZulu-Natal coast, followed by dolphins, Cape gannets and Bryde's whales.

fete.title: Kaapse Klopse, Cape Town carnival
fete.text: Every 2 January, up to 13,000 minstrels in bright costumes parade through Cape Town: the "second New Year".

Allemagne.name: Germany
hello: the northern “hi”, good at any time of day
food: Fischbrötchen
A bread roll filled with herring or smoked mackerel, down at the harbour.
Allemagne.respect: Recycling is taken seriously and beaches often charge a fee in summer (Kurtaxe).

sea.title: The Wadden Sea
sea.text: With the tides, mudflats stretch along 500 km of coast. Walking the seabed at low tide (Wattwandern) is popular, e.g. near Borkum.

fete.title: Kiel Week
fete.text: Begun in 1882 with 20 yachts, it is one of the world's largest sailing events and ends with a fireworks display.

Angola.name: Angola
hello: “hi”, and bom dia in the morning
food: Muamba de galinha
Chicken slow-cooked in palm oil with okra.
Angola.respect: Ask before photographing people or official buildings. Travel with a local contact on long dirt roads.

sea.title: Luanda Island and the nzimbu
sea.text: On this sandy spit off Luanda, the Portuguese gathered nzimbu, sea snail shells that served as currency in the Kongo region.

fete.title: Luanda Carnival
fete.text: In February, groups parade along the Nova Marginal to semba and kazukuta, with themes of music, nature or history.

Argentine.name: Argentina
food: Asado
The Argentine barbecue, a Sunday ritual.
Argentine.respect: Mate is shared: only take it when it’s handed to you, and say gracias only when you don’t want any more.

sea.title: Whales of Península Valdés
sea.text: UNESCO-listed in 1999, it hosts a major southern right whale breeding ground, from May to December.

fete.title: The Grape Harvest Festival
fete.text: In Mendoza, a wine and grape-harvest festival with parades; first official edition in 1936.
src: Wikipédia (EN), Fiesta Nacional de la Vendimia

Aruba.name: Aruba
food: Keshi yena
A ball of cheese stuffed with spiced chicken, baked in the oven.
Aruba.respect: Sunscreens containing oxybenzone are banned to protect the reefs.

fete.title: Aruba Carnival
fete.text: From early January to Fat Tuesday, with a grand parade on the last Sunday; it began in the 1950s.

Australie.name: Australia
hello: the Australian “hello”, often followed by mate
food: Seafood barbecue
Grilled prawns and fish, with a cold beer at sunset.
Australie.respect: Swim between the red and yellow flags, patrolled by the lifesavers. Never drop in on a local’s wave.

sea.title: The Budj Bim eel traps
sea.text: The Gunditjmara built channels and weirs to trap eels, a system up to 6,600 years old. World Heritage since 2019.

fete.title: Vivid Sydney
fete.text: Three weeks of light: installations, building projections and concerts, since 2009.

Autriche.name: Austria
hello: “hi”, Austrian style, for both hello and goodbye
food: Alpine lake trout
Caught in the lakes and grilled, often served with parsley potatoes.
Autriche.respect: Alpine lakes are often lined with private or paying beaches: look for signposted public access.

sea.title: Lake Neusiedl
sea.text: About 1 m deep and ringed by reeds, this steppe lake is the 'Sea of the Viennese', popular for sailing and windsurfing. UNESCO 2001.

fete.title: Salzburg Festival
fete.text: Founded in 1920, it runs about five weeks of music and drama, with Mozart operas and Jedermann on the cathedral square.

Bahamas.name: Bahamas
hello: “hello”, said with the islands’ sing-song accent
food: Conch salad
A salad of raw conch marinated in lime, with peppers and chilli.
Bahamas.respect: Don’t collect live conch and respect the protected fishing seasons.

fete.title: Junkanoo
fete.text: A parade of masks, drums and dance; inscribed on UNESCO's intangible heritage list in 2023.

Barbade.name: Barbados
food: Flying fish and cou-cou
Spiced flying fish with okra cornmeal, the national dish.
Barbade.respect: Wearing camouflage clothing is banned on the island. Swimwear on the beach only.

sea.title: Flying fish, the national dish
sea.text: Cou-cou and flying fish is the national dish; on Friday nights the Oistins fish fry draws locals and visitors.

fete.title: Crop Over
fete.text: Celebrates the end of the sugarcane harvest, climaxing with Kadooment Day in early August.

Belize.name: Belize
food: Rice and beans
Rice and red beans cooked in coconut milk, with chicken or fish.
Belize.respect: The barrier reef is fragile: touch nothing, don’t feed the fish and choose a licensed operator.

sea.title: The Belize Barrier Reef
sea.text: UNESCO-listed in 1996, the reef runs about 300 km along the coast; Cousteau made the Great Blue Hole famous in 1970.

fete.title: Garifuna Settlement Day
fete.text: A public holiday centred on Dangriga: parades, music and dance mark the Garifuna people's settlement in Belize.

Bonaire.name: Bonaire
food: Fried fish with funchi
Grilled or fried fish with a local cornmeal polenta.
Bonaire.respect: The Nature Fee is compulsory to dive or swim in the marine park. No gloves and no contact with the reef.

sea.title: A pioneering marine park
sea.text: Founded in 1979, Bonaire National Marine Park has 86 public dive sites, many reachable from the shore.

fete.title: Dia di Rincon
fete.text: Rincon's day: flag raising, performances and a parade celebrating the end of harvest (Simadan), since 1989.

Brésil.name: Brazil
hello: “hi, how are you?”, to which you reply tudo bom
food: Moqueca
A fish stew with coconut milk and palm oil.
Brésil.respect: Don’t bring out your valuables on the beach and share the waves: surfing is a religion here.

sea.title: The jangada, sailing raft
sea.text: In the Northeast, the jangada is a wooden sailing raft with a triangular sail, built without nails, crewed by 3 to 5 fishers.

fete.title: Carnival
fete.text: Before Lent, samba schools parade at Rio's Sambadrome over four nights.

Cambodge.name: Cambodia
hello: “hello” in Khmer, with palms pressed together
food: Amok
A coconut-milk fish curry cooked in a banana leaf.
Cambodge.respect: Cover your shoulders and knees in pagodas and never touch someone’s head.

sea.title: The Tonlé Sap’s changing flow
sea.text: Each year the Tonlé Sap River flows into the lake for six months, then back out. Floating villages live from fishing.

fete.title: Bon Om Touk
fete.text: Three days of dragon boat races in Phnom Penh at the end of the monsoon, when the Tonlé Sap reverses.

Canada.name: Canada
hello: “hi”, or bonjour depending on the province
food: Wild salmon
Grilled on a cedar plank, a Pacific coast tradition.
Canada.respect: Store your food out of reach of bears and learn about the First Nations territories you pass through.

sea.title: Haida canoes
sea.text: Renowned seafarers, the Haida carved canoes and travelled from Haida Gwaii as far as present-day Washington State.

fete.title: Quebec Winter Carnival
fete.text: Winter festival with Bonhomme Carnaval and the Ice Palace; held every year since 1955.

Cap-Vert.name: Cape Verde
hello: “hi”, followed by a sorriso (smile): that’s morabeza, the local hospitality
food: Cachupa
A stew of corn, beans and fish or meat, an everyday dish.
Cap-Vert.respect: Life here is stress-free: morabeza is met with patience. Keep your distance from the turtles nesting at night.

sea.title: Cidade Velha, Atlantic port
sea.text: Founded in the 15th century on Santiago, the first European colonial town in the tropics, UNESCO 2009; a place of memory of the slave trade.

fete.title: Baía das Gatas Festival
fete.text: Since 1984, three days of music on the beach at Baía das Gatas (São Vicente), nicknamed "Africa's Woodstock".
src: Wikipedia, Festival de Baía das Gatas

Chili.name: Chile
food: Empanadas de mariscos
Pastries filled with seafood and cheese.
Chili.respect: The Pacific is cold and powerful: wear a thick wetsuit and respect the locals at the points.

sea.title: The palafitos of Chiloé
sea.text: On the Chiloé archipelago, stilt houses typical of Chilote architecture line the water in Castro and Chonchi.

fete.title: Fiestas Patrias
fete.text: Cueca dancing, fondas and ramadas, empanadas, kites and traditional games around 18 September.

Chine.name: China
food: Hainan seafood
Crab, prawns and Wenchang chicken, the stars of the island.
Chine.respect: Carry your passport with you and set up a mobile payment method: cash is used less and less.

sea.title: Cormorant fishing
sea.text: On the Li River near Guilin, a loose snare holds the larger fish a cormorant brings back. The practice is over a thousand years old.

fete.title: Dragon Boat Festival
fete.text: Dragon boat races and zongzi, rice dumplings in leaves. Listed by UNESCO in 2009.

Chypre.name: Cyprus
hello: “hello” in Greek, in the south of the island
food: Grilled halloumi
A sheep’s and goat’s milk cheese that grills without melting.
Chypre.respect: Turtle nesting beaches are closed at night in summer: no torches and no parasols planted near the nests.

sea.title: The Kyrenia ship
sea.text: This 4th-century BC Greek merchant wreck, carrying wine and amphoras, was found in 1965 by a diver. It is shown in Kyrenia Castle.

fete.title: Limassol Carnival
fete.text: Ten days of costumes and satire, with the Carnival King and a grand parade of over 150 floats on Makariou Avenue.

Colombie.name: Colombia
food: Pescado frito con patacones
Fried fish, smashed plantains and coconut rice on the coast.
Colombie.respect: Avoid joking about the country’s violent past: Colombians are proud of their country as it is today.

fete.title: Barranquilla Carnival
fete.text: Four days before Ash Wednesday, with the Battle of Flowers and marimondas; UNESCO-listed in 2003.

Corée du Sud.name: South Korea
hello: a polite “hello”, with a slight bow
food: Hoe and market seafood
Raw fish sliced to order, eaten on the spot at the harbour market.
Corée du Sud.respect: Don’t start eating before your elders and don’t stick your chopsticks upright in your rice.

sea.title: The haenyeo of Jeju
sea.text: The haenyeo, “sea women”, free-dive down to 20 m to gather abalone and seaweed. Their craft has been UNESCO-listed since 2016.

fete.title: Boryeong Mud Festival
fete.text: Since 1998, Daecheon Beach hosts mud pools, mud slides and body painting, ending with fireworks.

Costa Rica.name: Costa Rica
hello: “pure life”, used as hello, thank you and goodbye
food: Casado
A full plate: rice, beans, plantain, salad and fish or meat.
Costa Rica.respect: Don’t feed the monkeys and respect the turtle nesting beaches, which are closed at night.

sea.title: Tortuguero, green turtle beach
sea.text: At Tortuguero, green, leatherback, loggerhead and hawksbill turtles nest, mostly February to July, with regulated access.

Croatie.name: Croatia
food: Black risotto (crni rižot)
A cuttlefish-ink risotto, a speciality of the Dalmatian coast.
Croatie.respect: In the old towns, don’t walk around shirtless or in swimwear: some municipalities hand out fines.

sea.title: The Betina gajeta
sea.text: In Betina on Murter island, the gajeta, a 5-8 m wooden sailboat, is still built, a craft protected as Croatian intangible heritage.

fete.title: Sinjska alka
fete.text: Riders gallop down a 160 m course aiming lances at a hanging iron ring, a tournament of 1715, UNESCO-listed in 2010.

Cuba.name: Cuba
food: Ropa vieja
Shredded beef stewed in tomato, served with rice and black beans.
Cuba.respect: Stay in a casa particular to support families, and carry cash: internet and bank cards remain hit-and-miss.

sea.title: Havana's Malecón
sea.text: An 8 km seawall begun in 1901 to protect the city from the sea; at night, families still fish from it.

fete.title: Santiago de Cuba Carnival
fete.text: Around July 18-27, with comparsas and congas; its roots go back to 18th-century summer festivities.
src: Wikipédia (EN), Carnival of Santiago de Cuba

Curaçao.name: Curaçao
food: Stoba
A goat or beef stew slow-cooked with spices.
Curaçao.respect: Shore diving is king: enter the water at the marked access points and don’t touch the coral.

sea.title: The Underwater Marine Park
sea.text: On the south coast, the Underwater Marine Park stretches 20 km, with up to 30 m visibility for divers.

Danemark.name: Denmark
food: Smørrebrød
Open rye-bread sandwiches topped with herring, prawns or egg.
Danemark.respect: The dunes are protected: stay on the boardwalks and don’t camp outside designated sites.

sea.title: Roskilde's Viking ships
sea.text: Around 1070, five Viking ships were sunk in the fjord to block the way to the town. Found in 1962, they are shown in Roskilde.

fete.title: Roskilde Festival
fete.text: Started in 1971 and run as a non-profit, it is one of Europe's largest music festivals, with over 130,000 attendees.

Djibouti.name: Djibouti
Djibouti.langs: Somali and Afar are the most widely spoken mother tongues; Arabic is also important.
hello: "peace be upon you"; the reply is "wa alaykumu s-salam"
food: Lahoh
A pancake-like bread similar to injera, eaten at breakfast with tea (shaah) or coffee (buna).
Djibouti.respect: About 98% of people are Muslim: start by greeting with "as-salamu alaykum".
baseSrc: Wikipédia, Culture de Djibouti et Cuisine djiboutienne

sea.title: The dhow, Red Sea sailboat
sea.text: A wooden sailboat with a trapezoid sail born in the Red Sea, the dhow serves for fishing, coastal trade and transport, from Djibouti to Madagascar.

fete.title: Fest'Horn
fete.text: Every year in mid-December, Fest'Horn celebrates music in Djibouti.

Dominique.name: Dominique
food: Callaloo
A soup of dasheen leaves and coconut milk.
Dominique.respect: Buy the nature sites pass and leave the whales and dolphins in peace, with a licensed operator.

sea.title: Sperm whales all year
sea.text: A group of sperm whales lives in the island's waters all year, drawing whale-watching visitors.

fete.title: World Creole Music Festival
fete.text: Three days of Creole music in Roseau on the last weekend of October, since 1997.

Égypte.name: Egypt
hello: “peace be upon you”, the everyday greeting
food: Cumin-grilled fish
Picked from the stall and grilled in front of you, with rice and salads.
Égypte.respect: Don’t touch or stand on the coral, use mineral sunscreen and keep your distance from the dolphins.

sea.title: The Nile felucca
sea.text: An Arab sailboat of 8 to 13 m carrying about ten passengers, the felucca is typical of the Nile and also seen on the Red Sea and eastern Mediterranean.

fete.title: Sham el-Nessim
fete.text: At the start of spring, Egyptians of all faiths picnic outdoors, often along the Nile, and dye boiled eggs.

Émirats arabes unis.name: United Arab Emirates
food: Machboos
Spiced rice with fish or meat, flavoured with dried lime.
Émirats arabes unis.respect: Away from the beaches, covering up is expected, and public displays of affection are frowned upon.

sea.title: Pearl diving in the Gulf
sea.text: Before oil, pearls fed Eastern Arabia: divers, captains (nakhuda) and crews set out to sea for months, peaking around 1912.

fete.title: Al Dhafra Festival
fete.text: Run by the Abu Dhabi Heritage Authority, it has camel contests, traditional souks and a date auction.

Équateur.name: Ecuador
food: Ecuadorian ceviche
Prawns marinated in lime in a tomato sauce, served with toasted corn.
Équateur.respect: In the Galápagos, stay two metres from the animals and always follow your naturalist guide.

sea.title: The Spondylus divers
sea.text: The Manteño culture dived for Spondylus, a purple and orange shell used as currency and traded as far as Mexico.

fete.title: Inti Raymi
fete.text: Andean winter solstice festival, observed on June 22 in Ecuador and linked to the sanjuanito.

Espagne.name: Spain
hello: “hi”, followed by a buenos días in the morning
food: Tapas
Small plates to share at the bar, from ham to fried squid.
Espagne.respect: People eat late, often after 9 pm. In the water, wait your turn and avoid paddling against the flow of the locals.

sea.title: Tower of Hercules
sea.text: In A Coruña, this Roman lighthouse from the late 1st century is the only one preserved and still used at sea. UNESCO since 2009.

fete.title: Las Fallas of Valencia
fete.text: Satirical ninot monuments are burned at the end of the festival, UNESCO-listed in 2016, alongside parades and brass bands.

États-Unis.name: United States
hello: “hi”, often followed by a how’s it going?
food: Fish tacos
Grilled or fried fish, cabbage and a creamy sauce, the emblem of surf towns.
États-Unis.respect: A tip (15 to 20%) is part of the price at restaurants. Respect the line-up pecking order: never drop in on anyone.

sea.title: Santa Cruz, 1885: three princes surf
sea.text: In 1885, three young Hawaiian princes surfed the mouth of the San Lorenzo River in Santa Cruz on redwood boards.

fete.title: Mardi Gras in New Orleans
fete.text: Carnival season opens on January 6 and peaks on Mardi Gras; krewe parades have run since 1856.
src: Wikipédia (EN), Mardi Gras in New Orleans

Fidji.name: Fiji
food: Kokoda
Raw fish marinated in lemon and coconut milk.
Fidji.respect: When visiting a village, cover your shoulders and knees, take off your hat and offer kava to the chief (sevusevu).

sea.title: The drua double canoe
sea.text: This double-hulled sailing canoe could reach 30 m and carry over 200 people. A new drua was launched in 2016.

fete.title: Hibiscus Festival
fete.text: In Suva, a float parade and the crowning of Miss Hibiscus. The first edition was in 1956.

Finlande.name: Finland
food: Salmon soup (lohikeitto)
Salmon, potatoes and dill in a creamy broth.
Finlande.respect: In the sauna, you go in naked or in a towel depending on local custom, and shower first. Quiet and personal space are highly valued.

sea.title: Kvarken, land rising from the sea
sea.text: Since the Ice Age the land has risen about 10 mm a year at Kvarken, among the fastest on Earth: over 5,600 small islands, UNESCO-listed.

fete.title: Vappu
fete.text: Helsinki's Havis Amanda statue gets a student cap, people wear student caps, drink homemade sima and eat tippaleipä funnel cake.

France.name: France
hello: the word that opens every door, even at the bakery
food: Seafood platter
Oysters, whelks and prawns, to share on a terrace facing the sea.
France.respect: Say bonjour when you walk into a shop and respect the priority rules in the water: the surfer closest to the peak goes first.

sea.title: Cordouan, a lighthouse at sea
sea.text: 7 km offshore, Cordouan lighthouse (1584-1611) became a UNESCO site in 2021. It is the last inhabited lighthouse in France.

fete.title: Dunkirk Carnival
fete.text: Born from the party held for sailors leaving to fish herring off Iceland, it fills the town with costumed bands led by a music clique.

Gambie.name: The Gambia
Gambie.langs: English is the official language; Mandinka (the largest ethnic group), Wolof, Pulaar, Serer and Jola are also spoken.
hello: "peace be upon you"; the reply is "wa alaykumu s-salam"
food: Domoda
A peanut stew with meat or fish and vegetables, regarded as the national dish.
Gambie.respect: About 96% of people are Muslim: start by greeting with "as-salamu alaykum".

sea.title: Kunta Kinteh Island
sea.text: Some 30 km from the mouth of the Gambia River, the former James Island (UNESCO, 2003) is a place of memory of Atlantic trade.

fete.title: Kartong Festival
fete.text: In the coastal village of Kartong, near Casamance, this annual week-long festival brings together dance and music.

Ghana.name: Ghana
hello: “welcome” in Twi, which you’ll hear often
food: Fufu and fish soup
A cassava and plantain dough to dip into a spicy soup.
Ghana.respect: Greet people before asking for anything and use your right hand to give or receive.

sea.title: Cape Coast Castle
sea.text: A fortified Gold Coast trading post, Portuguese from 1555 then Swedish, UNESCO-listed in 1979: a place of memory of the Atlantic slave trade.

fete.title: Homowo
fete.text: Among the Ga of Accra, Homowo recalls an old famine: its name means "to hoot at hunger". It opens with the planting.

Grèce.name: Greece
hello: “hello”, said with a smile to the taverna owner
food: Grilled octopus
Marinated in olive oil and oregano, dried in the sun outside the tavernas.
Grèce.respect: Cover your shoulders and knees to visit monasteries. Don’t pick up stones or ancient fragments.

sea.title: The caique fishing boat
sea.text: This wooden boat, often white with bright strakes, has long fished the Aegean and Ionian seas. Some now run island excursions.

fete.title: Patras Carnival
fete.text: A city treasure hunt, a grand parade of satirical floats and costumed groups, and the Carnival King burned at the port.

Grenade.name: Grenada
food: Oil down
A stew of breadfruit, salt fish and coconut milk.
Grenade.respect: Nutmeg is the island’s pride: buy directly from the cooperatives. Pay the underwater park fee.

sea.title: The Underwater Sculpture Park
sea.text: Opened in 2006 in Molinere Bay, it holds over 65 sculptures by Jason deCaires Taylor, cast from local people.

fete.title: Spicemas
fete.text: Grenada's Carnival, in August, to the beat of soca, calypso, kaiso and reggae.

Guadeloupe.name: Guadeloupe
food: Accras de morue
Spicy salt-cod fritters, to nibble with a drink before dinner.
Guadeloupe.respect: Say hello to everyone, even in passing. Don’t walk on the seagrass beds and watch turtles from a distance.

sea.title: The saintoise, boat of Les Saintes
sea.text: Designed in Les Saintes by Breton shipwrights, this sailing boat became a sport after the first Tour de Guadeloupe in 2001.

fete.title: Guadeloupe Carnival
fete.text: From the first Sunday of January to Ash Wednesday, with weekly parades; King Vaval is burned at the end.

Guatemala.name: Guatemala
food: Pepián
A spiced stew with toasted seeds, a national dish with Mayan roots.
Guatemala.respect: Ask before photographing local people, especially in Mayan villages.

sea.title: Livingston, reached by boat
sea.text: A Garifuna town at the mouth of the Río Dulce, Livingston has no road link: you arrive by boat from Puerto Barrios.

Honduras.name: Honduras
Honduras.langs: Spanish, Creole English on the islands
food: Baleada
A flour tortilla filled with beans, cream and cheese.
Honduras.respect: On the Bay Islands, pay the marine park fee and don’t collect coral or conch.

sea.title: Roatán, beside the great reef
sea.text: Roatán sits on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the world's second largest; Roatán Marine Park has guarded it since 2005.

fete.title: La Ceiba Grand Carnival
fete.text: On the third or fourth Saturday of May, a big float parade on Avenida San Isidro and street parties.

Hong Kong.name: Hong Kong
food: Dim sum
Small steamed bites, shared over tea.
Hong Kong.respect: On lifeguarded beaches, swim inside the shark-net enclosure and respect the flags.

sea.title: Hong Kong’s boat families
sea.text: Boat families (Tanka) long lived and fished from boats, notably at Aberdeen, Cheung Chau and Tai O.

fete.title: Dragon Boat Races
fete.text: Over 4,500 paddlers race in Victoria Harbour. The 2026 edition was the 50th.

Hongrie.name: Hungary
food: Lángos
Fried flatbread topped with sour cream and cheese, the king of Balaton’s beaches.
Hongrie.respect: On Lake Balaton, respect the storm warning lights: the wind can pick up very quickly on this shallow lake.

sea.title: Lake Balaton
sea.text: Central Europe's largest lake (600 km²) is shallow, 3.3 m on average, with sailing and fishing at resorts like Siófok and Keszthely.

fete.title: Busójárás in Mohács
fete.text: Masked busós parade through Mohács with music and dancing to end the winter. The festival has been UNESCO-listed since 2009.

Îles Caïmans.name: Cayman Islands
food: Cayman-style fish
Snapper or wahoo stewed with peppers, onions and tomatoes.
Îles Caïmans.respect: The marine parks are protected: no fishing and no anchoring outside designated spots. With the stingrays, follow your guide’s instructions to the letter.

sea.title: Stingray City
sea.text: Since the 1980s divers have fed squid to stingrays here; the rays now gather all year round.

fete.title: Pirates Week
fete.text: An 11-day festival launched in 1977 to energise the low season, with costumes and events across the islands.

Îles Cook.name: Cook Islands
hello: “may you live long”, the local greeting
food: Ika mata
Raw fish marinated in lemon and coconut milk.
Îles Cook.respect: Rāui protects certain areas of the lagoon: no fishing or collecting where it applies.

sea.title: Te Au o Tonga
sea.text: This 22 m double-hulled canoe, built in 1994, teaches Polynesian navigation. It has been based in Aitutaki since 2002.

fete.title: Te Maeva Nui
fete.text: Around 4 August, the islands compete in friendly rivalry with performances and food in Rarotonga.

Îles Salomon.name: Solomon Islands
food: Fish in coconut milk
Fresh lagoon fish cooked in coconut milk, with taro.
Îles Salomon.respect: Almost all land and reefs are customary: ask the village for permission and pay the diving or surfing fees.

sea.title: Marovo Lagoon
sea.text: About 700 km² of lagoon enclosed by a double barrier reef. Residents fish there and carve ebony.

Îles Turques-et-Caïques.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
food: Conch fritters
Conch fritters, the speciality of the archipelago.
Îles Turques-et-Caïques.respect: Don’t collect conch or coral, and don’t feed the rays or fish in the marine parks.

sea.title: Salt and conch
sea.text: Salt was a major export for years; local cooking is built on conch, in fritters or salad.

Îles Vierges britanniques.name: British Virgin Islands
hello: “hello”, said with the islands’ sing-song accent
food: Fungi and fish
Okra cornmeal with fish in Creole sauce.
Îles Vierges britanniques.respect: Use the marine park’s mooring buoys rather than your anchor and don’t touch the coral.

sea.title: The wreck of the RMS Rhone
sea.text: Sunk by the hurricane of 29 October 1867 off Salt Island, the Rhone lies in 9-26 m of water, a classic dive.

fete.title: BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival
fete.text: A regatta and sailing festival held since 1972 in one of the world's major sailing destinations.

Îles Vierges des États-Unis.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
food: Conch pâté
A fried pastry filled with spiced conch, sold at small stands.
Îles Vierges des États-Unis.respect: Sunscreens containing oxybenzone are banned to protect the reefs.

sea.title: Trunk Bay's underwater trail
sea.text: In the national park founded in 1956, a snorkeling trail follows Trunk Bay's coral reef.

Inde.name: India
hello: “I greet you”, with palms pressed together
food: Fish curry
A fish curry with coconut milk, a speciality of the west coast.
Inde.respect: Take off your shoes before entering a temple or a home, and eat with your right hand.

sea.title: The Kerala kettuvallam
sea.text: A wooden hull lashed with coconut fibre, it carried rice and spices from Kuttanad to Kochi port before becoming a houseboat.

fete.title: Nehru Trophy Boat Race
fete.text: On Punnamada Lake near Alappuzha, "snake boats" (chundan vallam) race every year since 1952.

Indonésie.name: Indonesia
hello: “good morning”; terima kasih means thank you
food: Nasi goreng
Spiced fried rice, often topped with an egg, for breakfast as well as dinner.
Indonésie.respect: Wear a sarong to enter a temple, give and receive with your right hand and don’t step on offerings placed on the ground.

sea.title: The pinisi of Sulawesi
sea.text: Around Bulukumba, shipwrights hand-build large wooden sailing ships called pinisi. This craft has been on UNESCO’s heritage list since 2017.

fete.title: Bau Nyale
fete.text: On Lombok, people gather nyale sea worms at night on Seger Beach, with songs, dances and boat races.

Irlande.name: Ireland
hello: “hello” in Irish, which always raises a smile
food: Seafood chowder
A creamy fish and seafood soup, served with soda bread.
Irlande.respect: At the pub, everyone buys a round in turn. On reef breaks, listen to the locals’ advice: the sea is powerful here.

sea.title: The currach, boat of the west
sea.text: Its wooden frame was once covered in hides, now tarred canvas. It is seen mostly on the west coast, including the Aran Islands.

fete.title: Puck Fair
fete.text: In Killorglin, Kerry, a wild goat is crowned 'King Puck' to open three days of horse fairs and festivities, traced back to 1613.

Islande.name: Iceland
food: Plokkfiskur
A fish and potato stew, served with rye bread.
Islande.respect: Stay on marked trails: moss takes decades to grow back. Check safetravel.is before every outing.

sea.title: Surtsey, an island born of the sea
sea.text: In 1963 an undersea eruption raised Surtsey off southern Iceland. UNESCO-listed in 2008, only a few scientists may land there.

fete.title: Þorrablót
fete.text: A midwinter dinner with speeches and poems, named for the month of Þorri. Its modern form dates from the 19th century.

Israël.name: Israel
food: Hummus and falafel
Chickpeas mashed with tahini and fried balls, served in pitta.
Israël.respect: During Shabbat, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, transport and shops slow right down: plan your journeys ahead.

sea.title: Acre, a port for millennia
sea.text: A port since the Bronze Age, Acre's old city keeps its Crusader halls and Ottoman walls. UNESCO-listed since 2001.

Italie.name: Italy
hello: “hi” and “bye”, best kept for people you know well
food: Spaghetti alle vongole
Pasta with clams, garlic and parsley, facing the sea.
Italie.respect: Cover your shoulders to enter a church and avoid wandering around town in your swimwear.

sea.title: The Venetian gondola
sea.text: Up to 11 m long and asymmetrical, it is moved by one oar resting on a carved forcola. An old Venetian law made it black.

fete.title: Venice Carnival
fete.text: Masks are documented since the 13th century: bauta, colombina, plague doctor. Banned in 1797, the carnival was revived in 1979.

Jamaïque.name: Jamaica
food: Jerk chicken
Chicken marinated in chilli and allspice, smoked over pimento wood.
Jamaïque.respect: Always ask before photographing anyone, and haggle with a smile.

sea.title: Port Royal, the sunken city
sea.text: On 7 June 1692 an earthquake and tsunami sank much of Port Royal, a privateer base; UNESCO listed it in 2025.

fete.title: Reggae Sumfest
fete.text: A major reggae festival in Montego Bay, held every year since 1993.

Japon.name: Japan
food: Kaisendon
A bowl of rice topped with the day’s raw fish, a harbour-town speciality.
Japon.respect: Leave no litter behind: public bins are rare, so carry a bag. No visible tattoos in some onsen.

sea.title: The ama free-divers
sea.text: Ama dive without tanks to gather abalone and seafood. Tradition says they have done so for about 2,000 years.

fete.title: Sapporo Snow Festival
fete.text: Every February, Sapporo shows snow statues and ice sculptures in Odori Park. The first edition was in 1950.

Jordanie.name: Jordan
food: Sayadieh
Fish and rice with caramelised onions, a speciality of Aqaba.
Jordanie.respect: Accept the tea you’re offered, it’s a sign of hospitality. Cover your shoulders and knees away from the beaches.

sea.title: Aqaba, Jordan's Red Sea port
sea.text: Jordan's only coastal city, Aqaba (ancient Ayla) has over 30 dive sites and fringing reefs stretching more than 25 km.

fete.title: Jerash Festival
fete.text: Founded in 1981 in the ancient city of Jerash, this festival of culture and arts hosts Jordanian, Arab and foreign artists.

Kenya.name: Kenya
hello: “hello”, to which you reply jambo sana
food: Fish in coconut milk (samaki wa kupaka)
Grilled, then coated in a spiced coconut sauce, a Swahili speciality.
Kenya.respect: On the Swahili coast, dress modestly in town and ask before taking photos.

sea.title: Lamu, a Swahili island town
sea.text: Founded around 1370, Lamu is Kenya's oldest continuously inhabited town. Its fort overlooks the seafront; a UNESCO site.

fete.title: Lamu Cultural Festival
fete.text: Each November, Lamu celebrates its heritage and coastal traditions in a festival with a carnival atmosphere.
src: The Star, A glimpse of Lamu Cultural Festival

La Réunion.name: Réunion
food: Rougail saucisse
Sausages simmered with tomatoes, onions and chilli, served with rice and beans.
La Réunion.respect: Swimming is regulated because of the shark risk: stick to authorised zones and the rules in force.

sea.title: Réunion's marine reserve
sea.text: Around the island, lagoons and drop-offs shelter over 1,200 fish species, protected by the marine nature reserve.

fete.title: Dipavali in Saint-Pierre
fete.text: Tamil families celebrate the festival of light: a parade of lit-up floats on the seafront, food, dance and music.

Liberia.name: Liberia
hello: “how are you?”, the best-known local greeting
food: Palm butter soup
A palm-nut stew, served with rice.
Liberia.respect: The Robertsport surf community is small and close-knit: introduce yourself, support the local schools and share the waves.

sea.title: The Kru mariners
sea.text: Renowned Atlantic fishers and navigators, the Kru were hired as free sailors on ships and settled along the West African coast.

Macédoine du Nord.name: North Macedonia
food: Ohrid trout
Caught in Lake Ohrid, an endemic species now protected and often replaced by farmed trout.
Macédoine du Nord.respect: Lake Ohrid is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: leave no litter and cover up to visit churches and monasteries.

sea.title: Lake Ohrid
sea.text: One of the world's oldest lakes (3-5 million years), 288 m deep, with over 200 endemic species. UNESCO-listed since 1979.

fete.title: Vevčani Carnival
fete.text: Traditional and modern costumes, masks and satire mark the Julian New Year; the carnival is claimed to be over 1,400 years old.

Madagascar.name: Madagascar
food: Romazava
A meat broth with brèdes, the local leafy greens.
Madagascar.respect: Respect the fady, local taboos specific to each region: ask for advice before swimming or visiting a sacred site.

sea.title: The Vezo, people of the sea
sea.text: On the west coast, the Vezo live from sea fishing. Their name means "the people who fish" and also "to struggle with the sea".

Malaisie.name: Malaysia
food: Nasi lemak
Coconut rice with sambal, fried anchovies and a hard-boiled egg.
Malaisie.respect: Away from the beaches, cover your shoulders and knees, especially in villages and near mosques.

sea.title: The Bajau Laut of Sabah
sea.text: Bajau Laut families live on houseboats and travel in groups. In Semporna, the Regatta Lepa celebrates these decorated boats.

fete.title: Rainforest World Music Festival
fete.text: Since 1998, three days of concerts and workshops at the Sarawak Cultural Village, at the foot of Mount Santubong.

Malawi.name: Malawi
food: Chambo
A fish from Lake Malawi, grilled or fried, served with nsima.
Malawi.respect: The lake is a nature reserve for its cichlids: don’t take any fish and dress modestly in the villages.

sea.title: Lake Malawi
sea.text: Africa's third-largest lake (580 km long), with clear water: about 800 described cichlid species, almost all endemic.

fete.title: Lake of Stars
fete.text: Since 2004, this three-day music festival has been held on the lake shore, with artists from Africa and Europe.

Maldives.name: Maldives
hello: the everyday greeting; kihineh? means “how are you?”
food: Garudhiya and mas huni
A tuna broth and a mix of tuna, coconut and chilli, for breakfast.
Maldives.respect: On inhabited islands, bikinis are for bikini beaches only, alcohol is banned and covering up is expected.

sea.title: The dhoni fishing boat
sea.text: The dhoni is the traditional fishing boat. Fishing is the country's second-largest industry, and fish with rice is the everyday meal.

Malte.name: Malta
hello: “good morning” in Maltese, a legacy of Italian
food: Pastizzi
Flaky pastries filled with ricotta or peas, to munch at the village café.
Malte.respect: Modest dress is required in the churches, which are numerous and busy. Don’t touch the Posidonia seagrass when snorkelling.

sea.title: The Maltese luzzu
sea.text: This colourful fishing boat has two eyes painted on its bow, said to protect fishermen. Marsaxlokk has the most luzzijiet.

fete.title: Maltese Carnival
fete.text: Celebrated since 1535, it centres on Valletta; in Nadur, on Gozo, a spontaneous carnival is known for satire and costumes.

Maroc.name: Morocco
hello: “peace”, the everyday greeting, to which you reply wa alaykoum salam
food: Fish tagine
Slow-cooked with preserved lemon, olives and vegetables, often shared from one dish.
Maroc.respect: Cover your shoulders and knees away from the beach, ask before photographing anyone and eat with your right hand.

sea.title: Essaouira, the city of winds
sea.text: A fortified Atlantic port since 1764 under Sultan Mohammed III, Essaouira's medina has been a UNESCO site since 2001.

fete.title: Gnaoua World Music Festival
fete.text: Since 1998, every June Essaouira brings Gnaoua musicians and guest artists from around the world together for shared concerts.
src: Wikipédia, Festival Gnaoua et Musiques du monde

Martinique.name: Martinique
food: Colombo
A Caribbean curry of chicken or goat, flavoured with colombo spice mix.
Martinique.respect: Greet people when you arrive and avoid beachwear in town. Turtles are for watching, not touching.

sea.title: The yole ronde
sea.text: A sailing boat born in the 17th century and built without plans; UNESCO listed the know-how in December 2020.

Maurice.name: Mauritius
food: Dholl puri
Split-pea flatbreads filled with curry, the island’s favourite street food.
Maurice.respect: Hindu temples are visited barefoot and with covered shoulders and knees. Don’t walk on the coral at low tide.

sea.title: Aapravasi Ghat, port of arrival
sea.text: Between 1834 and 1910, Indian indentured workers landed here in Port Louis. The site has been on the UNESCO list since 2006.

fete.title: Spring Festival (Chinese New Year)
fete.text: A public holiday in Mauritius, the Spring Festival follows the lunar calendar and falls in January or February.

Mayotte.name: Mayotte
food: Mataba
Pounded cassava leaves cooked in coconut milk.
Mayotte.respect: Mayotte is mostly Muslim: cover up away from the beach. The lagoon is a marine park, so watch turtles and dolphins from a distance.

src: Evaneos, Vocabulaire pour un voyage à Mayotte

sea.title: Mayotte's lagoon
sea.text: A coral barrier of about 160 km encircles one of the world's largest lagoons, with a rare double barrier in places.

Mexique.name: Mexico
food: Tacos de pescado
Fried or grilled fish in a corn tortilla, with lime and salsa.
Mexique.respect: In cenotes and on reefs, use only biodegradable sunscreen, or none at all as you’re often asked to.

sea.title: Sharing the catch: the Comcaac
sea.text: On the Gulf of California, the Comcaac custom canoaa an hant cooit lets anyone ask for fish from any returning boat.

fete.title: The Guelaguetza of Oaxaca
fete.text: On the two Mondays after July 16: costumed dances, food and crafts on Cerro del Fortín hill.

Micronésie.name: Micronesia
hello: “hello” in English, understood in every state of Micronesia, where each island has its own language
food: Grilled fish with breadfruit
Lagoon fish and breadfruit, the staple of island meals.
Micronésie.respect: Yap and Chuuk have strong customs: cover your thighs and ask before entering a village.

sea.title: Navigating without instruments
sea.text: Navigators from Satawal, like Mau Piailug, cross the ocean using stars, swells and birds.

fete.title: Yap Day
fete.text: Since 1968, dances, games, stone money and canoe building celebrate Yapese culture.

Monténégro.name: Montenegro
food: Njeguši ham
A smoked, air-dried mountain ham, served with local cheese.
Monténégro.respect: In old towns such as Kotor, people don’t walk around in swimwear.

sea.title: Perast and its artificial islet
sea.text: In the Bay of Kotor, the islet of Our Lady of the Rocks was built up by dumping rocks and sinking old stone-laden ships.
src: Wikipedia, Our Lady of the Rocks

fete.title: The Fašinada of Perast
fete.text: Each year residents go out in boats and throw stones into the sea to widen the islet, a custom tied to the legend of 1452.
src: Wikipedia, Our Lady of the Rocks

Mozambique.name: Mozambique
hello: “hi”, and bom dia in the morning
food: Piri-piri grilled prawns
Marinated in chilli and garlic, grilled over a wood fire.
Mozambique.respect: Watch whale sharks and manta rays without touching them, from a distance, with a responsible operator.

sea.title: Island of Mozambique
sea.text: Founded by the 14th century at the latest and a Portuguese port from 1507, this UNESCO island gave the country its name.

Namibie.name: Namibia
hello: “hello” in Afrikaans, understood all along the coast
food: Walvis Bay oysters
Farmed in the cold waters of the Benguela, among the most renowned in Africa.
Namibie.respect: Stay on authorised tracks: 4x4 tyre marks scar the desert for decades.

sea.title: The Skeleton Coast
sea.text: Fog, rocks and wrecks: its name comes from whale and seal bones. The San call it "the land God made in anger".

fete.title: Windhoek Karneval (WIKA)
fete.text: Ten days of German-style carnival in Windhoek: float parade, ball, beer festival and children's carnival.

Nicaragua.name: Nicaragua
food: Gallo pinto
Fried rice and beans, served morning, noon and night.
Nicaragua.respect: Many spots are on private land: use the authorised access points and respect the fishermen.

sea.title: Corn Islands, lobster islands
sea.text: On the Corn Islands, lobster and shrimp fishing became the main industry in the 1960s and 70s; crab soup is typical.

fete.title: Palo de Mayo
fete.text: An Afro-Caribbean dance and month-long May festival born in Bluefields on the Caribbean coast.

Norvège.name: Norway
food: Salmon and dried cod (tørrfisk)
Two treasures of the coast, from the smokehouse to the wooden drying racks.
Norvège.respect: Allemannsretten lets you camp in nature, away from houses, as long as you leave no trace. Fires are often banned in summer.

sea.title: Hurtigruten, the coastal route
sea.text: Since 1893, ships have linked Bergen and Kirkenes with 34 northbound calls, running daily all year round.

fete.title: Syttende mai
fete.text: National Day: children's parades with bands and flags since 1864, many people wearing the traditional bunad costume.

Nouvelle-Calédonie.name: New Caledonia
hello: “hello” in Drehu (Lifou), one of the 28 Kanak languages
food: Bougna
Yam, sweet potato, banana and chicken or fish cooked in coconut milk in banana leaves.
Nouvelle-Calédonie.respect: On customary land, perform the coutume: introduce yourself to the chief with a small offering before settling in.

sea.title: The lagoon and its barrier reef
sea.text: A barrier reef about 1,500 km long encloses the lagoon, UNESCO-listed in 2008. Dugongs and green turtles live there.

fete.title: Bourail Fair
fete.text: Since 1977, in Bourail: livestock shows, rodeo, crafts and local products, around 15 August.

Nouvelle-Zélande.name: New Zealand
hello: “hello” and “thank you” in Māori, used by everyone
food: Hoki fish and chips
Wrapped in paper and eaten on the beach.
Nouvelle-Zélande.respect: Respect Māori sacred sites (wāhi tapu) and the principle of kaitiakitanga, guardianship of nature.

sea.title: Māori waka
sea.text: Large waka taua reached 40 m with up to 80 paddlers. The waka hourua Te Aurere has crossed the Pacific using traditional navigation.

fete.title: Matariki
fete.text: The Māori New Year follows the rising of the Pleiades: stargazing and concerts. A public holiday since 2022.

Oman.name: Oman
food: Shuwa
Spice-marinated meat slow-cooked underground, for special occasions.
Oman.respect: Cover up away from hotel beaches, avoid public displays of affection and ask before taking photos.

sea.title: The dhow, sail of the Indian Ocean
sea.text: These trading sailboats long linked Arabia and East Africa on the monsoon winds; dhows are built and repaired in Sur, Oman.

fete.title: Muscat Festival
fete.text: In a large heritage village in Al Qurm Natural Park, you can see traditional Omani life, crafts and cultural shows.
src: Oman Ministry of Heritage and Tourism, Muscat Festival

Palaos.name: Palau
food: Grilled fish with taro
Fresh lagoon fish, served with taro.
Palaos.respect: The Palau Pledge, stamped in your passport, commits you to protecting the island. Reef-harmful sunscreens are banned.

sea.title: The Rock Islands
sea.text: Between 250 and 300 limestone islets, including a lake of stingless jellyfish found only in Palau. UNESCO-listed since 2012.

fete.title: Olechotel Belau Fair
fete.text: On Independence Day, each of the 16 states presents dances, chants, traditional dishes, carving and weaving.

Panama.name: Panama
food: Sancocho
A chicken soup with yuca and coriander, the national dish.
Panama.respect: In Indigenous territories such as Guna Yala, ask permission and pay the communities’ access fees.

sea.title: The Guna and their islands
sea.text: The Guna live mostly on small islands of Guna Yala, fish from hand-built dugout canoes and make molas.

Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée.name: Papua New Guinea
food: Mumu
Meat and vegetables steamed under hot stones.
Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée.respect: Reefs belong to the clans: surf camps pay a fee to the villages, which limit the number of surfers.

sea.title: The Milne Bay kula
sea.text: 18 island communities exchange red shell necklaces and white shell armbands by canoe, in opposite directions.

fete.title: Goroka Show
fete.text: Since 1956, about 100 tribes gather in Goroka to sing, dance and share their culture.

Pays-Bas.name: Netherlands
food: Raw herring (haring)
Served with onions, eaten tail-first at the market stalls.
Pays-Bas.respect: Cycle lanes have priority: look carefully before crossing, the bikes come fast.

sea.title: The Delta Works
sea.text: After the 1953 North Sea flood, dams, sluices and barriers were built until 1997. The Oosterschelde barrier closes only if the sea rises 3 m.

fete.title: King's Day
fete.text: The country turns orange and the vrijmarkt lets anyone sell used goods in the street without a permit or VAT.

Pérou.name: Peru
hello: “hi”, followed by a habla causa among friends
food: Ceviche
Raw fish marinated in lime and ají chilli, the national dish.
Pérou.respect: The caballitos de totora are a living heritage: admire them, and ask before photographing the fishermen.

sea.title: Caballitos de totora
sea.text: At Huanchaco, fishers ride reed boats made of totora, a tradition about 3,000 years old.

fete.title: Inti Raymi
fete.text: Winter solstice festival in Cusco: a staging of Inca rituals with 800+ performers at Sacsayhuamán.

Philippines.name: Philippines
food: Kinilaw
Raw fish marinated in coconut vinegar, ginger and chilli.
Philippines.respect: In marine protected areas, pay the access fees and don’t touch turtles or coral.

sea.title: The vinta of Mindanao
sea.text: This outrigger boat carries a sail striped in red, blue, green, yellow and white. The patterns often identify a family.

fete.title: Kadayawan
fete.text: In Davao, this festival gives thanks for nature’s gifts and showcases the region’s indigenous cultures.

Pologne.name: Poland
food: Pierogi
Dumplings filled with curd cheese, potatoes or meat.
Pologne.respect: On the Baltic, the dunes and pine forests are protected: stay on the marked paths down to the beach.

sea.title: Dar Pomorza, the White Frigate
sea.text: This 1909 full-rigger sailed round the world in 1934-35, the first Polish-flagged ship to do so. It is now a museum ship in Gdynia.

fete.title: Wianki in Kraków
fete.text: On the Vistula below Wawel Hill, flower wreaths are floated on the river, with concerts, a best-wreath contest and fireworks.

Polynésie française.name: French Polynesia
hello: “hello” in Tahitian, with a big smile
food: Poisson cru (raw fish in coconut milk)
Raw tuna marinated in lime, with crunchy vegetables and fresh coconut milk.
Polynésie française.respect: Marae are sacred sites: don’t climb on the stones. At Teahupoo, locals always have priority.

sea.title: Hawaiki Nui Va’a
sea.text: Outrigger canoe teams link Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a and Bora Bora over three days. More than a hundred teams take part.

fete.title: Heiva i Tahiti
fete.text: Dance, song and traditional sports around 14 July, a tradition that began in 1881. The name Heiva dates from 1985.

Porto Rico.name: Puerto Rico
hello: the joyful Puerto Rican exclamation, alongside the classic hola
food: Mofongo
Mashed fried plantain with garlic, often topped with seafood.
Porto Rico.respect: On shallow reefs, go in and out through the channels the locals use to spare the coral and your feet.

sea.title: Mosquito Bay, the glowing bay
sea.text: On Vieques, dinoflagellates make the water glow blue when disturbed; Guinness named it the brightest bay in 2006.

fete.title: Calle San Sebastián Festival
fete.text: Third weekend of January in Old San Juan: crafts, concerts and the cabezudos parade; over 200,000 visitors.

Portugal.name: Portugal
hello: “hi”, rounded off with an obrigado (thank you) or obrigada depending on who is speaking
food: Grilled sardines
Served on a slice of country bread, especially in summer.
Portugal.respect: Life moves at a gentle pace: take time for a coffee at the counter and give way to locals at busy peaks.

sea.title: Aveiro's moliceiros
sea.text: These shallow pinewood boats raked moliço, a seagrass used as fertiliser, from the Ria de Aveiro lagoon. They are now its symbol.

fete.title: Porto's São João festival
fete.text: All night: grilled sardines, glowing balloons, fireworks and plastic hammers. Many walk to the coast to see the sunrise.
src: Wikipedia, Festa de São João do Porto

République dominicaine.name: Dominican Republic
food: La bandera dominicana
Rice, red beans and stewed meat, the flag on your plate.
République dominicaine.respect: Haggle with a smile and favour small local businesses.

sea.title: Whales of Samaná Bay
sea.text: Samaná Bay is an important humpback whale breeding area in the Caribbean, popular with whale-watchers.

fete.title: February Carnival
fete.text: In February, Carnival fills streets nationwide with parades, dancing, music and food festivals.
src: Wikipédia (EN), Culture of the Dominican Republic

Royaume-Uni.name: United Kingdom
food: Fish and chips
Fried fish and chips, eaten down by the harbour.
Royaume-Uni.respect: Queuing is sacred, at the counter as in the line-up. Always thank the driver when you get off the bus.

sea.title: The Cornish pilot gig
sea.text: This 9.8 m six-oared boat once took pilots out to ships. World championships have been rowed in the Isles of Scilly since 1990.

fete.title: Up Helly Aa, Shetland
fete.text: In Lerwick, hundreds of guizers march with torches, then throw them into a Viking galley that is burned to end the Yule season.

sea.title: Offshore fishing and marine reserve
sea.text: Deep-sea fishing is practised from Lorient, Flamands and Corossol; a marine reserve founded in 1999 protects reefs and turtles.

fete.title: Les Voiles de St. Barth
fete.text: A regatta gathering sailing yachts in April, among other spring races.

Saint-Martin.name: Saint Martin
hello: “hello” in Creole, or hello on the Dutch side
food: Accras and johnny cakes
Salt-cod fritters and small fried breads, between French and Caribbean culture.
Saint-Martin.respect: The nature reserve covers many of the islets: no anchoring on seagrass beds and no fishing.

sea.title: A 3,054-hectare reserve
sea.text: Created in 1998, the reserve protects reefs, seagrass and mangroves; the nearby shelf is a humpback whale breeding area.

fete.title: Grand-Case festival
fete.text: Each July 21, the Grand-Case festival includes a traditional sailing race.

Saint-Vincent-et-les-Grenadines.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
food: Roasted breadfruit and fried jackfish
The national dish, served at small local eateries.
Saint-Vincent-et-les-Grenadines.respect: In the Tobago Cays Marine Park, pay the entry fee and let the turtles swim without approaching them.

sea.title: Bequia, island of boatbuilders
sea.text: With cedar and a sheltered harbour, Bequia built and repaired wooden boats; the schooner Friendship Rose was built here.

fete.title: Bequia Easter Regatta
fete.text: A regatta and music festival, one of the island's busiest times of the year.

Sainte-Lucie.name: Saint Lucia
food: Green fig and saltfish
Green bananas and salt cod, the national dish.
Sainte-Lucie.respect: The Soufrière Marine Park charges an entry fee and bans fishing and contact with the coral.

sea.title: The Pitons, World Heritage
sea.text: On the southwest coast, Petit Piton (743 m) and Gros Piton (798 m) have been UNESCO-listed since 2004.

fete.title: Saint Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival
fete.text: A jazz and arts festival created in 1992 to extend the tourist season into May.
src: Wikipédia (EN), Saint Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival

Salvador.name: Salvador
food: Pupusas
Corn cakes stuffed with cheese and beans, served with curtido.
Salvador.respect: The coast’s surf communities are welcoming: buy local, share the waves and stay humble at the point breaks.

sea.title: La Libertad's pier
sea.text: La Libertad's pier, the country's first port (1869), doubles as a fish market; Punta Roca makes it the surf capital.

fete.title: Festival of the Hammocks
fete.text: In Concepción Quezaltepeque, the hammock festival runs between the first and second weekends of November, since 1989.

Samoa.name: Samoa
food: Oka
Raw fish marinated in lemon and coconut cream.
Samoa.respect: Sunday is for church and rest: avoid noisy swimming near villages. At dusk, respect sa, the prayer time.

sea.title: The fautasi
sea.text: This longboat, about 30 m long, is rowed by up to 50 people to a drum beat. Races take place in June.

Sénégal.name: Senegal
hello: “how are you?” in Wolof, to which you reply maa ngi fi
food: Thiéboudienne
Rice with fish and vegetables, the national dish, shared from a large bowl.
Sénégal.respect: Greetings are long and important: take time to ask how people are before getting down to business.

sea.title: Saint-Louis and its fishers
sea.text: Founded in 1659 on a river island (UNESCO, 2000), Saint-Louis keeps a strong fishing tradition, notably in Guet Ndar.

fete.title: Saint-Louis Jazz Festival
fete.text: Since the early 1990s the city has swung to jazz, with bands from Saint-Louis, then Dakar, and guest artists.
src: Wikipédia, Festival international de jazz de Saint-Louis

Seychelles.name: Seychelles
food: Coconut fish curry (cari coco)
A mild coconut-milk curry, served with rice and chatini.
Seychelles.respect: Turtles and coco de mer are strictly protected. Don’t collect any shells from the beaches.

sea.title: Aldabra, the tortoise atoll
sea.text: A UNESCO site since 1982, the world's largest raised atoll shelters the largest population of giant tortoises in Seychelles.

Sierra Leone.name: Sierra Leone
food: Grilled fish and jollof rice
The day’s fresh fish and spicy red rice, on the peninsula’s beaches.
Sierra Leone.respect: Ask before photographing anyone and support the community’s small businesses and surf schools.

sea.title: Bunce Island
sea.text: On the Rokel estuary, this fort built around 1670 is a place of memory of the Atlantic slave trade; many African Americans have ancestors here.

Slovénie.name: Slovenia
food: Bled kremšnita
A vanilla cream cake, the speciality of Lake Bled.
Slovénie.respect: Nature parks such as Triglav are strictly protected: no wild camping and no drones without a permit.

sea.title: The Sečovlje salt pans
sea.text: Working since the 13th century, these salt pans still make Piran salt the traditional way. They are a landscape park and Ramsar wetland.

fete.title: Kurentovanje in Ptuj
fete.text: Kurents in sheepskin and big bells make noise to chase winter away. Their door-to-door rounds were UNESCO-listed in 2017.

Sri Lanka.name: Sri Lanka
hello: “long life”, said with palms pressed together
food: Rice and curry
Rice surrounded by several vegetable and fish curries and coconut sambol.
Sri Lanka.respect: Never pose with your back to a Buddha statue for a photo, and cover your shoulders and knees in temples.

sea.title: The stilt fishermen
sea.text: Near Weligama, fishermen plant a pole in chest-deep water and, perched on a crossbar, cast bamboo rods past the surf.

fete.title: Sinhala New Year (Aluth Avurudda)
fete.text: Two public holidays around 13-14 April: families gather and most shops close for about a week.

Suède.name: Sweden
hello: “hi”, pronounced “hey”, good at any time of day
food: Seafood smörgåsbord
Pickled herring, gravlax salmon and prawns on crispbread.
Suède.respect: Allemansrätten lets you camp for a night in nature, away from houses, leaving no trace and lighting no fires in dry spells.

sea.title: The Vasa, a 17th-century warship
sea.text: Sunk on its maiden voyage in Stockholm in 1628, the Vasa was raised in 1961 largely intact and can be visited at the Vasa Museum.

fete.title: Midsommar
fete.text: People dance in rings around a flower-decked pole, wearing flower wreaths, with pickled herring, new potatoes and strawberries.

Suisse.name: Switzerland
hello: “hello” in Swiss German; bonjour or buongiorno depending on the region
food: Fondue and perch fillets
Two classics of the Swiss lakeshores, for sharing.
Suisse.respect: Punctuality matters, and so does recycling. On the lakes, respect the swimming zones and boat traffic.

sea.title: Lake Geneva's Belle Époque steamers
sea.text: Eight paddle steamers built between 1904 and 1927 still sail Lake Geneva; the fleet has been a listed historic monument since 2011.

fete.title: Fête des Vignerons
fete.text: In Vevey on Lake Geneva, a huge show celebrates winegrowing; UNESCO-listed in 2016, the first Swiss tradition on the list.

Taïwan.name: Taiwan
food: Night markets
Squid skewers, oyster omelettes and bubble tea.
Taïwan.respect: In temples, enter through the right-hand door and leave through the left, without stepping on the thresholds.

sea.title: The Tao people’s tatala boats
sea.text: The Tao of Orchid Island build plank boats painted red, white and black and decorated with wave motifs.

fete.title: Lantern Festival
fete.text: Giant lanterns everywhere, and in Pingxi thousands of sky lanterns covered in wishes are released.

Tanzanie.name: Tanzania
hello: “hello” in Swahili, with a hakuna matata thrown in
food: Zanzibar spiced pilau
Rice fragrant with cloves and cardamom.
Tanzanie.respect: In Zanzibar, which is mostly Muslim, cover your shoulders and knees away from the beaches, especially in Stone Town.

sea.title: Stone Town, Zanzibar
sea.text: A UNESCO site since 2000, it blends Arab, Persian, Indian and European influences; its carved wooden doors are famous.

fete.title: Mwaka Kogwa
fete.text: In Zanzibar this Shirazi New Year is held in July: the "year's bath", with a playful fight using banana stalks.

Thaïlande.name: Thailand
hello: “hello”, with ka for a woman and khrap for a man
food: Tom yam goong
A hot and sour soup with prawns, lemongrass and galangal.
Thaïlande.respect: Never touch someone’s head, don’t point your feet at a Buddha and cover up in temples.

sea.title: The longtail boat
sea.text: A car engine on a pivoting pole, a propeller at the end of a long shaft: the design began in Sing Buri in the 1930s.

fete.title: Loy Krathong
fete.text: At full moon, people float a krathong, a small banana-leaf basket, on the water and make a wish.

Tonga.name: Tonga
food: Ota ika
Raw fish marinated in lemon and coconut milk.
Tonga.respect: Sunday is sacred by law: no swimming and no sport. Cover your shoulders in town.

sea.title: The kalia double canoe
sea.text: In the 18th century the kalia reached 35 m, with two unequal hulls and a movable mast. It could carry over 100 people.

fete.title: Heilala Festival
fete.text: A week of culture and music in Nuku’alofa around the king’s birthday on 4 July.

Tunisie.name: Tunisia
food: Fish couscous
A recipe from the Tunisian coast, spiced up with harissa.
Tunisie.respect: Away from the beaches, covering up is appreciated. During Ramadan, avoid eating in public during the day.

sea.title: Charfia fishing
sea.text: In Kerkennah, fixed palm-frond traps catch fish in waters one to two metres deep; sea plots are leased at auction.

fete.title: Carthage International Festival
fete.text: Since 1964, music, theatre and dance every summer at the ancient theatre of Carthage, by the sea.

Turquie.name: Turkey
food: Balık ekmek
A grilled fish sandwich, sold right on the quays.
Turquie.respect: Cover your shoulders and knees and take off your shoes to visit a mosque; women cover their hair.

sea.title: The Turkish gulet
sea.text: This two-masted wooden sailing vessel, 14-35 m long, is built mainly in Bodrum and Marmaris, and famed for 'blue cruises'.

fete.title: Kırkpınar oil wrestling
fete.text: In Edirne, wrestlers in leather shorts pour olive oil over themselves and compete for three days. UNESCO-listed in 2010.

Uruguay.name: Uruguay
food: Chivito
The national sandwich, filled with beef, ham, egg and cheese.
Uruguay.respect: Sharing mate is a gesture of friendship: don’t stir the bombilla and hand it back to the person serving.

sea.title: Isla de Lobos sea lions
sea.text: Off Punta del Este, the island holds a huge sea lion and fur seal colony and an 1858 lighthouse 59 m high.

fete.title: Candombe Llamadas
fete.text: A candombe drum parade in Montevideo during Carnival; candombe was UNESCO-listed in 2009.

Vanuatu.name: Vanuatu
food: Lap-lap
A yam or cassava paste cooked in leaves in a stone oven.
Vanuatu.respect: Many beaches are customary land: ask permission and pay the small access fee the village asks for.

sea.title: Gaua’s Water Music
sea.text: On Gaua in the Banks Islands, women perform Water Music. The show, about 30 minutes long, can be seen in Lembot village.

Venezuela.name: Venezuela
food: Arepa
A corn cake with any filling you like, from fish to cheese.
Venezuela.respect: Check the local situation before you go and choose posadas run by local people.

sea.title: Los Roques Archipelago
sea.text: A national park since 1972, Los Roques has about 350 islands and cays; fishers from Margarita settled there long ago.

Vietnam.name: Vietnam
food: Bánh xèo
A crispy pancake with prawns, to roll up in fresh herbs.
Vietnam.respect: Take off your shoes when entering someone’s home and avoid sticking your chopsticks upright in your rice.

sea.title: The thúng chai basket boat
sea.text: This small round boat of woven bamboo is waterproofed with resin and coconut oil, and coastal fishers still use it.

fete.title: Tết Trung Thu
fete.text: Children’s festival at full moon: lantern parades, mooncakes and lion dances.

Wallis-et-Futuna.name: Wallis and Futuna
Wallis-et-Futuna.langs: Wallisian (’Uvean), Futunian and French are the official languages.
food: Taro and yam
Taro, yams and sweet potatoes are the staples; fish is widely eaten along Uvea’s coast.
Wallis-et-Futuna.respect: Custom matters a great deal, and the kava ritual is important, especially on Futuna. Observe before joining in.

sea.title: The outrigger race
sea.text: The outrigger canoe race, called fakatete on Wallis and kumete on Futuna, is now a water sport.
